newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: STRIKE HELD UP GOLD FIELDS NAMIBIA RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: STRIKE HELD UP GOLD FIELDS NAMIBIA RESULTS.

text.p: Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said on Monday that it was forced to delay posting results for the quarter ended September due to disruption resulting from a recent six week strike at its Tsumeb Corp Ltd (TCL) .
Gold Fields said results would be published when reliable results became available.
"Results would only be available once we can gain access to reliable information at TCL," a Gold Fields spokeswoman said.
It reitereated that preliminary planning anticipated that after completion of the repairs to the smelting complex, production at TCL mines should commence in December.
A cash shortfall until sales resumed would be met from internal resources and an insurance claim related to the cost of repairs and loss of revenue had been lodged, Gold Fields said.
It added that all the necessary agreements, arrangements and technical and financial plans for a viable operation were being put into place.
The bitter dispute over wage increases ended last week when Tsumeb Corp Ltd and the Mineworkers Union of Nambia (MUN) agreed on a 10.5 percent wage increase.
Owners Gold Fields of Namibia, said earlier this month the strike is estimated to have cost N$50-100 million.
